subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<skillKey>.enabled: false` become a hard read/exec access boundary, or remain a prompt/status visibility setting while a separate capability-grant model handles enforcement?
rationale: Both choices are plausible but compatibility-sensitive: the security request aligns with safe defaults, while changing existing `enabled:false` semantics affects operator expectations and multiple execution surfaces.

options.title: Make disabled skills deny access
options.body: Treat `enabled:false` as an enforceable deny boundary for the skill directory and add upgrade-facing docs/tests for read, write/edit/apply_patch, exec, and sandbox paths.

options.title: Route through capability grants
options.body: Keep `enabled:false` visibility-only and require the broader capability-manifest/grant model in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12678 before enforcing per-skill runtime access.

options.title: Document trusted-code model
options.body: Leave disabled skills as prompt/status filtering and document that skill folders remain trusted host code unless operators restrict filesystem and exec access separately.

recommendation.title: Make disabled skills deny access
recommendation.body: Treat `enabled:false` as an enforceable deny boundary for the skill directory and add upgrade-facing docs/tests for read, write/edit/apply_patch, exec, and sandbox paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Current history and related security-capability discussions point to steipete as the best available owner for the security-boundary product decision.
